tasks.short: Design and explain how we grade, promote, pay and assess people, now ready for pay transparency.

today.trigger: A policy review, a new CAO, the coming pay transparency law, or an HR Director request.
steps: Collect current rules from SharePoint policies, the CAO and AFAS job schemes
Compare with practice in the sector and with what the law will require
Draft a method note (promotion criteria, pay step rules, review cycle)
Discuss with HR Director, HR Business Partners and the works council
Write the final policy and explain it to managers
drudgery: Hunting for the latest version of each policy
Rewriting the same rule for office, warehouse and driver groups
today.time_sinks: Collecting and reconciling scattered rules, and redrafting after each round of comments.

lenses.faster: A model gathers the current rules from SharePoint, the CAO and AFAS into one comparison and drafts the method note; the specialist spends the time on choices and consultation, cutting the task by about a quarter.
lenses.autonomous: Not autonomous: a policy request starts it and a draft pack is assembled, but every method choice is made by the specialist and the HR Director, and system changes go to the works council.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the HR Director: before each policy decision, a one-page impact view showing which groups (office, warehouse, drivers, flex) each option touches; demand would grow if cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses searching for policy versions; the specialist wants more time on testing whether rules are fair and understandable.
lenses.options: Two or three method variants (for example promotion on tenure plus skills versus skills only) with their cost and group effects change which one the HR Director and works council choose.
lenses.altitude: The week shifts from writing policy text to choosing between costed options and preparing works council consent; the job becomes more expert in pay design and labour law.
reach: Take over the HR Business Partners' first draft of policy notes for their sites; needs coaching on site realities
Absorb the HR Director's preparation of works council consent requests; needs WOR knowledge

tasks.human_edge: Judging what the works council, the CAO parties and the shop floor will accept, and weighing fairness against cost, stays with the person.
tasks.pattern_why: Method design is open-ended and political; the model helps gather and draft, the specialist leads.

in_practice.trigger: Policy review request logged by the HR Director or a new legal or CAO requirement.
steps: Model pulls current policies, CAO clauses and AFAS job scheme fields into a comparison table
Model drafts a method note with two or three options and their group effects
Specialist edits, chooses the proposal and costs it in Excel
HR Director and works council review; specialist publishes the final policy on SharePoint
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist and HR Director approve the method; works council consent where WOR 27 applies.
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint policy library with version history and the decision note

evidence.claim: Pay transparency requires a job evaluation method on four factors and works council consent on system, criteria and grouping.
A pay or grading system needs works council consent unless a CAO settles it.
General-purpose assistants can draft policy comparisons and notes.

risks: Draft method copies outside practice that does not fit the CAO
Policy text drafted by a model reads well but hides a cost effect
research_questions: How many policy reviews per year does the specialist run and how long does gathering take today?
Does the works council accept model-drafted option notes as a basis for consent?
Which parts of the method are already fixed by the CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer and the warehouse CAO?

tasks.short: Run the appraisal cycle and the equal pay checks, soon the yearly pay gap report.

today.trigger: The yearly appraisal and pay round, and from 2027 the pay transparency gap report.
steps: Prepare appraisal forms and timelines for managers
Export pay and job data from AFAS into Excel
Calculate pay differences between men and women per job group
Explain findings to HR Director and agree actions
Follow up with managers on missing appraisals
drudgery: Rebuilding the same gap calculation in Excel each year
today.time_sinks: Manual data cleaning and chasing; flex worker pay data from agencies is not in AFAS.

lenses.faster: Gap figures and appraisal status come from a fixed calculation on the AFAS extract, so cleaning and chasing mostly go; programme design and follow-up stay, about a third faster.
lenses.autonomous: Nightly AFAS refresh recalculates gaps per job group and appraisal completion; the specialist reviews outliers and the HR Director signs off before anything is reported.
lenses.ambitious: Flex workers served for the first time: agency pay data from the three portals joins the gap view, which the law will require anyway; demand would grow if cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses chasing appraisal forms or rebuilding spreadsheets; the specialist wants more time explaining gaps and fixing their causes.
lenses.options: Scenario runs of how much each correction (raise, regrade, step change) closes a gap change which correction the HR Director picks within budget.
lenses.altitude: The week moves from building the report to explaining each pay difference and proposing corrections; the specialist gains the right to flag a group for joint evaluation preparation; more expert.
reach: Take over the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's gap dashboard upkeep; needs Power BI basics
Absorb the HR Administrators' appraisal reminders; needs nothing new

tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a difference is explained by objective factors and agreeing actions with the works council needs judgement and trust.
tasks.pattern_why: Gap calculations and completion tracking follow written rules; the programme design around it stays with the person.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract refresh and the yearly reporting deadline.
steps: Script calculates pay gaps per job group and gender, flags gaps of 5% or more
Script lists missing appraisals per manager and sends reminders
Specialist reviews flagged groups and records an explanation or action
HR Director approves the report and actions
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist checks each flagged gap; HR Director approves before reporting or sharing with the works council.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI report snapshot and a SharePoint register of explanations and actions

evidence.claim: Yearly reporting, first over 2027 pay; agency workers count; a 5%+ unexplained gap triggers a joint evaluation with the works council.
AFAS Profit 8 stores job schemes and categories as preparation for pay transparency.

risks: Agency pay data incomplete or late, so the gap is wrong
Gender data quality in AFAS too poor for small groups (AVG minimisation also applies)
research_questions: Can the three agencies deliver pay per worker in a usable format?
How many job groups at Noordhaven are too small to report without identifying people?
How much of today's effort is chasing appraisals versus analysing them?

tasks.short: Keep the staff handbook and pay-related records in AFAS current.

today.trigger: A CAO change, a new policy, a yearly indexation, or an audit finding.
steps: Read the CAO change or policy decision
Find every handbook section and AFAS field it touches
Rewrite handbook sections in Word and upload to SharePoint
Update job scheme and pay scale records in AFAS
Tell HR Administrators and Payroll what changed
drudgery: Finding every place a rule is mentioned
today.time_sinks: Cross-checking that handbook, AFAS and payroll all say the same thing.

lenses.faster: A model finds each affected section and drafts the changes in tracked mode, and a script checks AFAS scale tables against the CAO table; the specialist reviews, saving about half.
lenses.autonomous: A new CAO text or policy decision in SharePoint starts it; drafts and a mismatch list are prepared without the specialist, who approves each change before publishing.
lenses.ambitious: Warehouse and transport shift staff served for the first time with a short Dutch and English (and Polish) handbook version on their phones; demand would grow if cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses retyping scale tables; the specialist wants more time making rules clear for shop-floor staff.
lenses.options: Little; the content follows the CAO and policy.
lenses.altitude: The specialist stops editing documents and owns one source of pay rules that handbook, AFAS and payroll draw from; slightly more expert.
reach: Absorb HR Administrators' handbook upkeep; needs SharePoint page skills
Take over Payroll Specialist's scale table check after indexation; needs AFAS payroll table knowledge

tasks.human_edge: Reading what a CAO clause means for Noordhaven's own groups and choosing wording staff will understand stays with the person.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns a CAO or policy change into tracked handbook edits that the specialist can check line by line.

in_practice.trigger: New CAO text, policy decision or indexation uploaded to SharePoint.
steps: Model lists affected handbook sections and drafts tracked edits
Script compares AFAS pay scale tables with the CAO table and lists mismatches
Specialist approves edits and corrects AFAS records
Change note goes to HR Administrators and Payroll
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves each edit and each AFAS change before publishing.
data_needed: AFAS job schemes and pay scales
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history and AFAS change log

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 holds job schemes and categories as structured fields.
Models can draft tracked edits to policy documents from a change text.

risks: Model misses one place a rule appears, leaving conflicting texts
research_questions: How many handbook changes per year and how long each takes today?
Are AFAS scale tables exportable for automatic comparison?
Would shift staff actually read a phone version?

tasks.short: Make org charts, career path and pay analysis reports from AFAS data.

today.trigger: Requests from the HR Director, Finance or managers, and the yearly pay round.
steps: Export headcount, jobs and pay from AFAS
Clean and combine in Excel
Draw org charts and career path overviews in PowerPoint or Visio
Write a short summary
Send to the requester
drudgery: Redrawing org charts after every change
Cleaning the same export each time
today.time_sinks: Manual data cleaning and chart layout.

lenses.faster: Org charts, grade distributions and career paths are generated from the nightly AFAS extract and a model writes the summary; the specialist checks, saving about 60%.
lenses.autonomous: Nightly refresh rebuilds the standard reports; a request starts a custom cut; the specialist reviews only new or unusual reports.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to site managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo: a monthly view of grade spread and career steps for their warehouse staff; demand would grow if cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses redrawing org charts; the specialist wants more time on what the numbers mean.
lenses.options: Little; reports describe the current state.
lenses.altitude: The specialist moves from producing reports to defining which views exist and answering the questions they raise; slightly more expert.
reach: Take over part of the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's report building; needs Power BI modelling
Absorb FP&A Analyst's headcount-by-grade cuts; needs budget structure knowledge

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which view answers the real question and spotting data that looks wrong because of a reorganisation stays with the person.
tasks.pattern_why: Charts and tables follow fixed rules on AFAS data; a short model summary is optional.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract refresh or a report request.
steps: Power BI rebuilds org chart, grade spread and career path views
Optional model call drafts a short text summary
Specialist checks new or changed reports
Report is shared via Power BI or SharePoint
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist reviews any new report type and any summary before it goes to managers.
in_practice.logs_to: Power BI refresh history and access log

evidence.claim: Noordhaven already runs Power BI on a nightly AFAS extract.
Generated org charts and dashboards from HR data are standard BI practice.

risks: Pay data shown to managers who should not see it (AVG)
Org data in AFAS out of date, so charts mislead
research_questions: Which reports are requested more than twice a year?
Is the manager hierarchy in AFAS reliable enough for automatic org charts?
Who may see pay-level detail per site?

tasks.short: Research what jobs require, how jobs relate, and how roles in logistics are changing.

today.trigger: A new or changed role, a regrading request, or the yearly job architecture review.
steps: Read current job descriptions and AFAS job data
Interview managers and job holders
Look at sector sources and CAO job descriptions
Map how the job relates to others in the family
Write findings
drudgery: Comparing similar job descriptions line by line
today.time_sinks: Desk research and comparing many job texts.

lenses.faster: A model compares job descriptions, groups near-duplicate jobs and summarises sector trends; interviews and conclusions stay, saving about a third.
lenses.autonomous: Not autonomous: a regrading request starts a research pack, but the specialist decides what changed.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: a yearly check of all job descriptions for drift, flagging only roles whose core accountabilities materially changed; demand would grow if cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses line-by-line text comparison; the specialist wants more time on the shop floor seeing how jobs are done.
lenses.options: Two or three job family maps (for example warehouse roles split by equipment versus by responsibility) change how the job architecture is set up.
lenses.altitude: From answering single regrading requests to owning the job family map for all three sites; more expert.
reach: Absorb the Recruiters' job description drafting for new vacancies; needs Recruitee templates
Take over the L&D Specialists' mapping of required certificates per job; needs Studytube data

tasks.human_edge: Observing the work, hearing what managers leave out and judging whether accountabilities really changed stays with the person.
tasks.pattern_why: Research steps vary per job; the specialist leads and uses the model for comparison and summarising.

steps: Model compares the job with similar jobs and flags overlap and gaps
Model summarises sector sources and CAO job descriptions
Specialist interviews manager and job holder
Specialist writes findings
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist decides whether accountabilities materially changed.

evidence.claim: 61% of employers are rewriting job descriptions for AI; 49% say salary structures lag (opt-in survey).
Advice not to regrade unless core accountabilities materially changed.
CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer parties are regrading sector jobs.

risks: Over-flagging drift creates regrading requests that are not warranted
Sector summaries cite outdated or wrong sources
research_questions: How many job descriptions are older than three years?
How many regrading requests arrive per year?
Will the sector regrading settle the driver and warehouse jobs anyway?

tasks.short: Build the questionnaires and forms we use to analyse and grade jobs.

today.trigger: Start of a job evaluation project or a gap in current materials, now the pay transparency four factors.
steps: Review current job analysis forms
Decide what the factors and questions should be
Draft questionnaires and interview guides in Word
Test with a few managers
Finalise and store on SharePoint
drudgery: Rewording questions for different job families
today.time_sinks: Drafting and redrafting questions per job family.

lenses.faster: A model drafts questionnaires per job family on the four factors and a per-factor grade draft with reasons; the specialist tests and decides, saving about 40%.
lenses.autonomous: Not autonomous: drafts are prepared on request; every instrument is approved by the specialist and the works council where it is part of the grading system.
lenses.ambitious: Flex workers and night shifts served for the first time with a short phone questionnaire in their language feeding job analysis; demand would grow if cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses formatting forms; the specialist wants more time testing whether questions measure what they should.
lenses.options: Variants of factor weighting and question sets change which grading system goes to the works council.
lenses.altitude: From maintaining forms to owning the evaluation instrument the whole pay structure rests on; more expert, with a legal edge.
reach: Absorb the People Analytics Analyst's survey setup; needs Forms and basic survey design
Take over HR Business Partners' interview guides for job reviews; needs nothing new

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what counts as effort and working conditions in a warehouse, and checking for gender bias in questions, stays with the person.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns a job family and the four factors into a draft questionnaire that can be checked.

in_practice.trigger: Job evaluation project start or factor change.
steps: Model drafts a questionnaire per job family on skills, responsibilities, effort and working conditions
Model drafts per-factor grade suggestions with reasons from a job description
Specialist tests with three managers and edits
Instrument goes to the works council for consent
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves instruments; works council consents to the system and criteria.

evidence.claim: A UK university pilot scored 50 job descriptions with ChatGPT per HERA factor, over 70% agreement with experts.
Job evaluation on four factors with works council consent.
Grade recommendations by AI can be high-risk under AI Act Annex III 4(b) from December 2027.

risks: 30% wrong grade drafts become unexplained pay differences
AI Act high-risk duties if model grade suggestions are used
research_questions: Does the 70% accuracy hold on Dutch logistics job descriptions?
Which jobs fall inside CAO grading and so are out of scope?
Will the works council accept a model-assisted grading step?

tasks.short: Analyse pay, market and sector data and answer questions from management, CAO parties and government.

today.trigger: Pay round, CAO costing, a CBS or sector survey, or a management question.
steps: Collect AFAS data and market or sector data
Build analysis in Excel
Cost CAO or pay proposals
Write a note or fill in the survey
Present to HR Director or Finance
today.time_sinks: Combining sources and building one-off costing models.

lenses.faster: CAO costing becomes a reusable model on AFAS data and a model drafts market findings and survey answers; the specialist checks, saving about 35%.
lenses.autonomous: A survey or costing request starts a draft; nothing goes out without the specialist's check.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the Finance Director and FP&A: a costing of every CAO or pension change within a day, including flex cost via agency rates; demand would grow if cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses survey forms; the specialist wants more time advising on what the numbers mean for offers and retention.
lenses.options: Costing several CAO or pay scenarios side by side changes the position HR takes into negotiations.
lenses.altitude: From number-crunching to advising Finance and the HR Director on pay decisions with ready scenarios; more expert.
reach: Take over FP&A Analysts' personnel cost scenarios; needs budget model knowledge
Absorb the Controller's CBS wage survey submissions; needs CBS definitions

tasks.human_edge: Choosing comparators, judging market data quality and framing advice for negotiations stays with the person.
tasks.pattern_why: Questions vary; costing logic is fixed but findings and advice need the specialist in the lead.

in_practice.trigger: Costing request, survey deadline or management question.
steps: Costing model runs scenarios on AFAS data
Model drafts market findings or survey answers from sources
Specialist checks and adjusts
Note goes to HR Director or Finance
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves every figure and finding before it leaves HR.

evidence.claim: Compa Analyst Agent with Mercer data drafts market-pricing findings; no customer result published.
48% of employers say benchmarks miss AI skills.
Pensioenfonds Vervoer expects a new scheme on 1 January 2027.

risks: Market data unsuitable for Dutch logistics roles
research_questions: Which market data does Noordhaven license today?
How often is CAO or pension costing needed per year?
Does Compa or Mercer cover Dutch logistics jobs?

tasks.short: Train managers and HR colleagues on pay rules, bands and pay conversations.

today.trigger: New pay policy, pay round, pay transparency start, or new managers.
steps: Decide what managers need to know
Build slides and examples in PowerPoint
Set up a course in Studytube
Give sessions per site
Answer follow-up questions
drudgery: Answering the same questions after sessions
today.time_sinks: Material building and repeat sessions on three sites.

lenses.faster: A model drafts slides, cases and a Studytube module from the policy; the specialist edits and still teaches, saving about 30%.
lenses.autonomous: Not autonomous: drafting starts on a policy change, the specialist approves and delivers.
lenses.ambitious: Team leads on night shifts in Venlo and Tilburg trained for the first time through a short Studytube module with practice pay conversations; demand would grow if cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses building slides; the specialist wants more live practice with managers on hard pay conversations.
lenses.altitude: From delivering repeat sessions to coaching managers on difficult cases; slightly more expert in advice.
reach: Absorb part of the L&D Specialists' module building in Studytube; needs Studytube authoring
Take over HR Business Partners' manager briefings on pay rounds; needs nothing new

tasks.human_edge: Live coaching, reading the room and handling sensitive pay questions stays with the person.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns a policy into draft training material the specialist reviews.

in_practice.trigger: Published policy change or pay round start.
steps: Model drafts slides, cases and quiz questions from the policy
Specialist edits and loads the module into Studytube
Specialist runs live sessions per site
Questions feed an FAQ on SharePoint
in_practice.human_gate: Specialist approves all material before publishing.

evidence.claim: Pay transparency requires bands before negotiation and no salary-history question, which managers must learn.
A benefits or pay chatbot must say it is AI.
Models can draft training slides and quizzes from a policy.

risks: Material states rules wrongly and managers repeat them
Managers skip e-learning without live follow-up
research_questions: How many managers need pay transparency training before 2027?
What completion rates does Studytube show for non-mandatory courses?
Do night-shift team leads have time and devices for a module?

role.altitude: The specialist moves from producing reports, forms and handbook text to owning the job architecture and the evidence behind every pay difference, ready for pay transparency reporting and works council consent.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: pay gap and grade dashboards in Power BI
HR Administrators: handbook upkeep and appraisal reminders
FP&A Analysts: personnel cost and CAO scenarios
Recruiters: job descriptions and pay bands for vacancies
L&D Specialists: pay-related Studytube modules
role.ceiling_note: About 30-40% of the hours in these tasks can go; the limit is consent and consultation (works council, CAO parties), AI Act high-risk duties for grade or pay suggestions from December 2027, GDPR Art. 22, and incomplete agency pay data.
skills_to_grow: Job evaluation methods on the four pay transparency factors
Power BI and data modelling on AFAS extracts
WOR consent procedures and EU pay transparency rules
AI Act oversight and logging for high-risk HR uses
role.ambitious_version: A single job architecture for all three sites, including flex workers, where every pay difference has a recorded reason, gaps are watched monthly, and CAO or pension changes are costed within a day for the HR and Finance Directors.
